title: Unity GPU render tests require a graphics device
task_type: Unity Editor asset and build verification
environment: Applies to Unity GPU/image render tests. It does not apply to compile-only or other tests that do not render pixels; those may use `-nographics` if their requirements permit it.
goal: Run shader image comparisons from Unity batch mode.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Batch mode was treated as sufficient for headless GPU rendering, and `-nographics` was added to make the run non-interactive.
what_worked: Historical correction: Run GPU image validation with graphics enabled. Keep batch mode if useful, but omit `-nographics`; inspect the Unity log for the selected graphics device/backend before interpreting image failures. Verification reported by the source: The same GPU render suite was rerun with graphics enabled on the workstation's graphics adapter. Effect-specific image probes then passed; the remaining failure was independently traced to a missing nested mesh in a separate fixture.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: A GPU render validator produced many failing image checks when Unity was launched with `-nographics`. The editor log identified the active backend as Null Gfx, so the validator was not exercising the intended graphics path.
why: Confirmed: `-nographics` selected Unity's Null Gfx backend. That backend cannot provide the GPU rendering surface the image validator requires, so its failures were invalid evidence about shader output.
improved_method: For any Unity test that reads rendered pixels, do not pass `-nographics`. Confirm the log shows a real graphics backend before treating image comparisons as shader evidence.
when_to_use: Applies to Unity GPU/image render tests. It does not apply to compile-only or other tests that do not render pixels; those may use `-nographics` if their requirements permit it.
when_not_to_use: It does not apply to compile-only or other tests that do not render pixels; those may use `-nographics` if their requirements permit it.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
